summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of primary CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in remission was admitted for scheduled maintenance chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate. He tolerated the infusion well without significant side effects. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, reaching 0.10 by the morning of discharge, indicating effective clearance. His renal function remained stable throughout. However, hyponatremia worsened to 124 mEq/L, likely due to overuse of desmopressin for diabetes insipidus, which the patient admitted to using extra doses to reduce nocturia. Despite medical advice to remain for sodium recheck after Lasix administration, the patient declined and chose to be discharged home. Lisinopril was restarted for hypertension, and he was instructed to follow up on labs and continue temozolomide and seizure prophylaxis. The plan includes return in four months for the next chemotherapy cycle.
